analysis:
Examined all three supplied analyses against the canonical definition index and detailed T-041 contract. They consistently describe one change in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCache.swift: head 1772–1779 adds closed-cache checks and delegates oldest-entry eviction to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, retaining retireIndexedEntries as the deletion callback. No independently supported security regression can be established from these summaries alone; integration_source omits all six reviewed source units.
The material cross-file question is whether the helper preserves bounded progress past undeletable entries, stops on external storage changes or closure, and reports only indexed bytes actually freed to SSDDiskBudget. This affects T-041/TB-007 disk-budget and storage mitigations and provider availability (T-016, A-018). The summaries identify retirement ownership/root guards at base 1794–1803 and teardown at head 430–461, but their synchronization with the new helper cannot be validated without source. Review the helper, retirement implementation, and budget call sites together before concluding that eviction remains safe.
The analyses report unchanged scope-derived HMAC lookup, encryption/context bindings, donation limits, TTL, and staging-reservation release. They provide no evidence of new authorization, attestation, wire-encryption, plaintext-exposure, or billing behavior. Existing same-account timing and external-storage retention/replay risks in T-041 are not new findings. Missing replay and helper evidence remain coverage limits, not proof of a missing control or of safety.
